Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  September 4, 2025

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on September 4, 2025. Commissioner
Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Octavio
  Padilla - District 2 Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3,
  Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4, Commissioner Henry
  Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Parks, Recreation, and Community Services
  Mary Rouzan  Recreation Supervisor
  Kesha Brady  Food Services Manager
  Jack Mooring  Tree Maintenance Supervisor
  Ashley Ferrette  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner Padilla
that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on August 7, 2025,
be approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:

Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Padilla, McLemore, Beck, and Denmon
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Tree Maintenance Supervisor, Jack Mooring reported
the following: Parks Division - Park staff have installed new windscreens, benches, and
shade canopies at the pickleball courts in Darby Park. The small baseball field at Rogers
Park has been overseeded in preparation for the winter baseball season. New park rules
signs will be installed at the entrances of each park. Graffiti Division - In August, staff
experienced heavy activity in the following areas: Vincent Park, West Boulevard from Hyde
Park to Florence Avenue and District 3: on Arbor Vitae to the La Cienega corridor. Tree

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

Division – West Coast Arborist is wrapping up their annual contract and working on
projects at Water Treatment Plant, Vincent Park, Hillcrest Boulevard, Centinela Adobe
Museum, and Siminski Park. City crews are doing service requests along with additional
trimming projects on Manchester (palms), La Brea (ficus) and Centinela Adobe Museum.

REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor, Mary Rouzan reported the following:
Hispanic Heritage Festival - Join us on Saturday, September 20, from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. in
downtown Inglewood for the City’s annual Hispanic Heritage Festival. The festival is FREE
and will feature live performances by Frankie J, The Reel Band, Clave Dura, Los Garzas, and
Ballet Folklorico Macias. Additional attractions include a classic car show, health
screenings, children’s activities, and over 80 vendors and informational booths. There will
be a food court featuring delicious food from Fiesta Martin, Pupusa Ritas, Baja Fish Tacos,
Tamale Fiesta, Inglorious Funnels, and more. Be sure to mark your calendars and join us
for this exciting event! Early Learners Program Open House - The Early Learners Play to
Learn Program wrapped up a fantastic summer with its full-day Kiddie Camp at Siminski
Park, and half-day summer school classes at Rogers Park. The staff received lots of positive
feedback from parents, which was a great way to end summer and begin the fall season!
The first day of classes will be Tuesday, September 16. The Rogers Park location will
continue to offer two Parent and Me classes on Wednesdays and Fridays for students 12-
29 months of age, the Tiny Tots class on Tuesdays and Thursdays for children 24-35
months, and the Spanish Immersion class for preschool students ages 3-5. Lockhaven
Community Center and Siminski Park will also offer the Early Learners classes for preschool
students ages 3-5. We still have space for enrollment in the Parent & Me classes and at
our Lockhaven and Siminski locations. Please share with friends and family. Also launching
in October will be “Wonder Wednesdays,” a series of afternoon enrichment to provide
children with specialized classes such as Art, Music, Literacy, and Cooking that will
contribute to their overall development outside of the regular preschool curriculum. All
teachers and assistants are recharged and ready to begin another wonderful school year!
Youth Sports - The City of Inglewood's citywide youth sports division has wrapped up the
2024-2025 year in Youth Sports, offering flag football, volleyball, and soccer, track,
baseball, and softball leagues. The summer season of Dodgers Dreamteam baseball and
softball concluded last weekend with consolation games, third-place showdowns, and
championship battles. The 2025 season supported 22 teams, 5 age divisions, 26 coaches,
and 296 players. The season culminated with pizza parties, hot dogs, awards, and
championship rings for the division winners. All participants walked away with a positive
experience and a desire to do it all again next season. Special shout out to all the volunteer
coaches, field champions, and sports staff that work hard to create opportunities for
growth through sports with fun memories that will last a lifetime. Next up, Inglewood
Rams flag football season in the fall of 2025. The Inglewood Rams Player “Evaluation Clinic”
is this Saturday, September 6th to be conducted by the Los Angeles Rams staff. Volunteer
coaches will attend to evaluate and rate players as they prepare for the “Coaches Draft”

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

next week. Practices for the 2025 season begin the week of September 15th and games will
begin October 2nd. The league is excited to have over 250 participants with 32 female
players. Come out and support the action on Thursday evenings or all day on Saturdays.
For more information on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports website
at https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Food Services Manager, Kesha Brady,
reported on the following: Senior Center Operations - Our Senior Center continues to
experience significant growth, with notable increases in participation numbers and an
expanded range of programs. We have several exciting programs and classes for
September, starting with a new Tuesday dancercise class that will begin on September 2.
Mercedes Aguirre of the LA County Department of Mental Health will be conducting a
presentation on Emotional Well-being and Stress on September 25. A program has been
planned to honor Hispanic Heritage Month on Monday, September 15, beginning at 10:00
a.m. - 11:00 a.m. with special poetry readings. On September 11, we will screen the movie
"The Greatest Game Ever played" and a Dance from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. on September
25. On September 24, we will take seniors to Redondo Beach to enjoy an afternoon of fun
in the sun from 11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. On September 17, we will take seniors to the Getty
Museum. Senior Nutrition - The Senior Center serves approximately 460 seniors per week
through home-delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate meals. We
continue to offer fresh produce weekly in partnership with the Social Justice Learning
Institute, as well as monthly shelf-stable meal boxes in collaboration with the Los Angeles
Food Bank. Farmers' Market cards have been distributed, and seniors have been able to
take several trips to the market from the center through our transportation services. We
also work in partnership with Los Angeles County to refer seniors to our center to receive
Home Delivered Meals and workshops focused on healthy eating habits. As our numbers
continue to climb weekly in program participation, we look forward to serving all of our
seniors. Senior Center (Paratransit) - The City of Inglewood’s paratransit program
continues to provide trips to seniors and the disabled community in Inglewood and
Hawthorne. We are in the midst of transitioning our current two-way radio system to a
push-to-talk digital radio system. With this change, our radio communication system will
allow us to maintain and improve our service when it relates to communication. The better
our communication is, the better our service can be as well. Our goal is to reduce and or
eliminate areas where our current two-way radios do not cover. We aim to have the best
possible communication coverage that we can and as always, we continue to strive in
providing outstanding paratransit service to our seniors and disabled community.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation, and Community Service Department Director,
Thomas Uwal reported on the following: Community Newsletter (All Good in Inglewood)
- The All Good in Inglewood Department of Parks, Recreation and Community Services
newsletter will be released on October 1, 2025. This biannual publication serves as a vital

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

communication tool, designed to inform residents about upcoming programs, special
events, new classes, park updates, and recreational opportunities. By highlighting available
services, the newsletter fosters community engagement, promotes wellness, and
encourages active lifestyles for all members of the community. Relocation of Park
Maintenance Staff - The Park Maintenance staff currently housed at Edward Vincent Jr.
Park will be relocating to the City Service Center before October 1, 2025. The existing
building at Edward Vincent Jr. Park is outdated and no longer meets the operational needs
of the department. The City has long recognized the necessity for a modern facility to
better support staff and accommodate essential equipment. The Public Works
Department has completed the design phase for a new facility, with construction
scheduled to begin next year. Reopening of Pickleball and Tennis Courts at Darby Park -
Following the Pickleball Community Meeting on July 7, 2025, where players, city staff, and
public officials provided feedback, the City initiated a series of upgrades to the pickleball
and tennis courts at Darby Park. These enhancements reflect the City’s commitment to
improving recreational facilities and ensuring community voices are included in program
development. The reopening celebration will take place on Saturday, September 6, 2025,
featuring music, giveaways, and family-friendly activities. Community members are invited
to join us for what promises to be an enjoyable and engaging event. Fitness instructor
Althea Moses is retiring after 15 years of service with the City. We are expecting her at our
next commission meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Padilla met with Doris Obih (Program
Coordinator) and found that Pickleball has twice as many participants. Commissioner
Denmon suggested adding future Pickleball classes for kids.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:53 p.m.
